class_imbalance_explanation: In payment processing, successful transactions outnumber failures (~88% vs ~12%). Because of this class imbalance, a naive classifier predicting 'Success' for every transaction would still achieve ~88% accuracy while catching 0% of failures. Therefore, Precision, Recall, F1 Score on the Failure class, and balanced class weights are essential for evaluating operational utility.

feature_importance.label: Concurrent System Load
feature_importance.description: Active concurrent transactions per second across the platform. Loads above 20,000 req/s increase queue contention.

feature_importance.label: Server Processing Latency
feature_importance.description: Internal microservice orchestration and validation time. Values above 90ms indicate server processing contention.

feature_importance.label: Bank Gateway Latency
feature_importance.description: Response time from the upstream acquiring/issuing bank network. Values above 80ms correlate strongly with timeout failures.

feature_importance.label: User Network Latency
feature_importance.description: Round-trip network latency between the customer device and the FinPath edge gateway. Baseline mean is ~50ms.

feature_importance.label: Transaction Hour (0–23)
feature_importance.description: Hour of the day when the transaction was initiated. Peak evening hours (18:00–22:00) experience elevated concurrency.

model2.labeling_methodology_note: Synthetic Labeling Note: In this simulated dataset, failed transactions are labeled with the component ('User', 'Server', or 'Bank') exhibiting the highest raw latency during the transaction. This represents a synthetic heuristic rather than verified production trace root-cause attribution.
